 Metal Breakdown Daily: New Slipknot Album, Original W.A.S.P. Drummer Tony Richards Dies, Ronnie Radke Sued
 Clown says Slipknot's eighth album is coming and nobody at a label gets a vote; original W.A.S.P. drummer Tony Richards has died at 69; Ronnie Radke is reportedly being sued over a Hollywood Hills rental.
 By Scott Penfold - November 12, 2026 
 Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp 
 Clown says Slipknot’s eighth album is coming and no label gets a vote. Today’s Metal Breakdown Daily starts there. 
 Metal Breakdown Daily is one page, every weekday: the episode on the player below, the three stories in print. Today: Shawn Crahan tells Rock Sound “I can promise you, album eight’s coming out,” there’s enough for a ninth, and “no one’s telling us what to do anymore.” Tony Richards, the drummer on the first W.A.S.P. album, has died at 69. And Ronnie Radke is reportedly being sued for libel and slander over a Hollywood Hills rental. 
 Up next: Who Is In Slipknot Right Now? The Current Lineup 
 🎧 STREAM THE METAL BREAKDOWN DAILY NOW: 
 Scott Penfold opens today’s Metal Breakdown Daily with Clown’s promise that Slipknot’s eighth album is coming and what “a musician’s album” means from a band with no label in the room, then Tony Richards, the original W.A.S.P. drummer, and the lawsuit reportedly filed against Ronnie Radke. The Take: Slipknot with no adult supervision is the version worth hearing. Download the free Loaded Radio App on Apple iOS and Google Play and stream the show now. 
 Clown: “Album Eight’s Coming Out,” There’s Enough For A Ninth, And “No One’s Telling Us What To Do Anymore” 
 Shawn “Clown” Crahan told Rock Sound , on being inducted into the magazine’s Hall Of Fame, that Slipknot’s eighth album is coming (“I can promise you, album eight’s coming out”), that Corey Taylor has sung rough demos on “so many songs,” that the band has enough material for a ninth, and that for the first time “no one’s telling us what to do anymore.” 
 Crahan credits drummer Eloy Casagrande with the pace: he’s “forcefully feeding the machine,” and the sessions have been “effortless recording and fun.” On the volume of material: “So technically, I guess we could have a ninth too,” with a caveat he repeated: “I’m not telling you we’re doing that. I’m just telling you, number eight’s coming out.” The September standalone single “Arsenal” , the band has said, won’t be on it.
 The record is the first since The End, So Far closed out the Roadrunner contract in 2022, the first on the band’s own imprint, and the first without Sid Wilson and Craig Jones. Jim Root said earlier this year the writing was already underway ; Clown is the first to promise a finished product. His description: “I don’t think people are ready for what we’ve created because even we are saying we’ve gone to another level,” and “This new one is probably going to take people a little time because it’s long songs and definitely a musician’s album.”
 No release date, title or producer has been given. For a band that has changed members more than most , the lineup making this one is the story as much as the songs.

 Tony Richards, Original W.A.S.P. Drummer, Dies At 69; Blackie Lawless: “We Were Wounded In A Way We Never Really Quite Recovered From” 
 Tony Richards, W.A.S.P.’s original drummer and the drummer on the band’s 1984 self-titled debut, has died at 69, Blackie Lawless announced on the band’s social media on Wednesday, November 11: “The entire W.A.S.P. camp are deeply saddened to hear of the passing of our original drummer, Tony Richards.” No cause or date of death was given. 
 Richards joined in 1982, played on the debut, released August 17, 1984, and was reportedly fired at the start of the tour behind it, replaced by Steve Riley. Before W.A.S.P. he’d played in Dante Fox, the band that became Great White. Lawless, in his post: “When he was gone from the band we were wounded in a way that we never really quite recovered from.” He called Richards “absolutely equal to any of the others,” and has said as much before; four years ago: “When we lost him, we were mortally wounded, and we knew it.” The first album cover has all four faces on it; “Second and third albums are just me.”
 Catherine Holmes, Chris Holmes’s wife and manager, said Chris had been talking to Richards “every month for the last few years”: “His passing makes us sad. He deserved not to be forgotten along with what he brought to this industry.” Holmes’s own story is in the Mean Man documentary . Richards is the third former W.A.S.P. drummer to die, after Frankie Banali in 2020 and Steve Riley in 2023. The songs he played on, “I Wanna Be Somebody,” “L.O.V.E. Machine” and “Animal (F**k Like A Beast)” , are still the ones the band opens and closes with.
 Ronnie Radke Reportedly Sued For Libel And Slander Over A Hollywood Hills Rental 
 Falling In Reverse frontman Ronnie Radke is being sued for libel, slander and emotional distress by Jade Cheng, a chef and the CEO of Superhumn, according to a New York Post report cited by Lambgoat; the suit, which seeks unspecified damages, stems from a $3 million Hollywood Hills rental Radke leased in February through Cheng’s company and from statements he made about her afterward. 
 According to the report, Radke publicly accused Cheng of scamming him out of about $220,000 in connection with the rental and filmed himself at the property pointing out trash and damage he blamed on her. The lawsuit alleges he went further in posts and videos, calling her a con artist, making claims about her personal life and health, and suggesting she had committed crimes and that federal authorities were pursuing her. Videos cited in the filing reportedly include the lines “we’re coming for you” and “you’re going to get it.” Cheng disputes the accusations and calls them fabricated.
 Radke has not responded publicly, and the Post said it could not establish who was responsible for the property’s condition. None of the allegations, on either side, has been proven. The court was not named in the report. Radke’s public disputes have their own history on this site, from the Alex Terrible exchange to the Brittany Furlan restraining order ; this one is the first that starts with a lease.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by California Post (@californiapost) 
 The Take: Slipknot With No Adult Supervision Is The Version Worth Hearing 
 Clown says Slipknot’s eighth album is long songs and “a musician’s album,” that nobody at a label gets a say for the first time, and that people aren’t ready for it. Here’s what that means. 
 “A musician’s album” is the phrase that should worry you a little. It’s what bands say when the songs are seven minutes and the chorus is optional. Slipknot have earned the right to make that record, and they’ve also made albums praised as returns to form by people who stopped listening a month later.
 But every Slipknot album until now was made with someone in the building whose job was to ask for the single. That person is gone. Casagrande is the most dangerous drummer the band has had, and the man who built Slipknot’s whole visual world is telling you he’s surprised. I’d rather hear a band with no adult supervision overreach than hear The End, So Far again. If it takes people a little time, good. Iowa took people a little time , and it’s the one they’re all measured against .
 TL;DR 
 Clown told Rock Sound Slipknot’s eighth album is coming (“I can promise you”), there’s enough material for a ninth, Corey Taylor has sung rough demos, and “no one’s telling us what to do anymore.” No date, title or producer; “Arsenal” won’t be on it.
 Tony Richards, W.A.S.P.’s original drummer (1982–84, the 1984 debut), has died at 69. Blackie Lawless: losing him left the band “wounded in a way that we never really quite recovered from.” No cause given. He’s the third former W.A.S.P. drummer to die, after Frankie Banali and Steve Riley.
 Ronnie Radke is reportedly being sued for libel, slander and emotional distress by Jade Cheng over statements he made after accusing her of scamming him out of $220,000 on a Hollywood Hills rental. Cheng calls his accusations fabricated; Radke hasn’t responded; nothing is proven on either side.
 The Take: a Slipknot album with no label in the room is the version worth hearing, even if it overreaches.
 FAQ 
 Is Slipknot releasing a new album? 
 Yes, according to Shawn “Clown” Crahan, who told Rock Sound in November 2026: “I can promise you, album eight’s coming out.” He said the band has enough material for a ninth album, that Corey Taylor has recorded rough vocal demos on many songs, and that it’s “a musician’s album” with long songs. No release date, title or producer has been announced. The September 2026 single “Arsenal” will not be on it.
 Who is on the new Slipknot album? 
 Clown singled out drummer Eloy Casagrande as the driving force in the writing and said Corey Taylor has sung the demos. It’s the first Slipknot album since the departures of Sid Wilson and Craig Jones, and the first released on the band’s own imprint after The End, So Far (2022) completed their Roadrunner Records contract.
 How did Tony Richards die? 
 No cause of death has been given. Blackie Lawless announced on November 11, 2026 that Richards, W.A.S.P.’s original drummer, had died at 69. Richards played on the band’s self-titled 1984 debut and was replaced by Steve Riley at the start of the tour that followed. Before W.A.S.P. he was in Dante Fox, the band that became Great White.
 Why is Ronnie Radke being sued? 
 According to a New York Post report, Jade Cheng, a chef and CEO of Superhumn, has sued Radke for libel, slander and emotional distress over statements he made after accusing her of scamming him out of about $220,000 on a $3 million Hollywood Hills rental he leased through her company in February. The suit seeks unspecified damages. Cheng calls Radke’s accusations fabricated; Radke has not responded, and none of the claims on either side has been proven.
 Did Slipknot leave Roadrunner Records? 
 Yes. The End, So Far, released in 2022, was the band’s final album under its Roadrunner contract. Slipknot’s next album will be released through the band’s own imprint, which Clown described as the first time “no one’s telling us what to do anymore.”
